correctness.rationale: For one explicitly realized depth-five rooted binary tree and \(K=2,D=3\), the relevant first-three-row count matrix has determinant 1. Eliminating offset and positive scale yields \(R(t)=(1+t)/(1+2t^2)\). The identity \((s-t)[1-2(t+s+st)]=0\) exhausts all alternative real positive decay bases; \(s=(1-2t)/(2(1+t))\) is admissible exactly at \(0<t<1/2\), except the coincident fold at \((\sqrt6-2)/2\). Explicit positive parameter reconstruction yields identical three conditional Binomial laws, while \(\det J=2\beta_1t^3(2t^2+4t-1)\) isolates the singular fold. A feasible fourth observation gives a strictly decreasing ratio \((1-t^2)/(1+2t^2)\), proving global identification. The standalone standard-library CHECK.py passed tree realization, exact rational alias and additional rational tests. No finite experiment is used as proof of the universal statement.

The article does not state the counterexample or four-condition repair. The second inspected article explains generic discrete identifiability ambiguities for ODE systems, not this Binomial genealogy. Actual targeted literature and mathematical-record queries found no statement implying these specific results; exact historical uniqueness is not established.

value.rationale: The source models three parameters from a minimal three sampled genealogical events and asserts simple independent-count criteria suffice. A realizable full-rank design instead admits two distinct positive decay rates throughout a nonempty open interval, so ideal offspring probability observations alone cannot resolve biologically distinct parameters. The exact two-fold classification, singular Fisher fold and feasible sibling-only fourth observation both delimit the failure and provide a constructive sampling fix without presupposing larger sample sizes or new methods. This is a motivated experimental-design boundary in a current kin-dependent branching model, not a cosmetic parameter change.
